Wildfire report · NASA FIRMS VIIRS NOAA-21 data

Active fire detections worldwide from NOAA-21

The VIIRS instrument on the NOAA-21 satellite recorded vegetation-fire detections in countries this year. Africa's savannas account for more than half. The rest follow the seasons: South and Southeast Asia in spring, North America in July, Siberia in August, and Indonesia and the Amazon in September.

Where the fires were

Each cell is a 0.5° square (roughly 50 km at the equator); darker means more detections. Hover a cell for its count.

When the fires happened

Detections per week by continent. Africa dominates all year, with a northern savanna season in January and a larger southern one from June to September. Asia peaks twice: March and April in South and Southeast Asia, then August in Siberia. North America peaks in July.

Busiest days

Single days with the most detections. All ten fall between 6th August and 2nd September, at the height of the southern African dry season.

    Hotspots

    Key findings

    Reading this data

    • A detection is a hot pixel, not a fire. VIIRS sees 375 m pixels, so one large fire produces many detections over many days. Counts show where and when burning was concentrated, not how many separate fires there were.
    • Much of this is managed burning. Savanna fires in Africa, crop-residue burning in South and Southeast Asia, and land clearing in Indonesia and the Amazon are usually set on purpose. The data does not say whether a fire was a wildfire or a planned burn, so readings of the seasonal patterns here are inferences from timing and location.
    • Likely industrial heat sources were removed. This file has no label for gas flares, volcanoes or factories. Instead, any spot about 2 km across that showed heat on at least 70 of the 277 days was treated as a fixed source, since vegetation fires rarely burn that long in one place. That removed detections, mostly in Russia, Iran, China, Iraq, India, the US, Algeria and Libya, which fits oil and gas flaring. A long-burning peat fire could also be caught by this filter.
    • One satellite. NOAA-21 passes over most places once in daylight and once at night. of detections are daytime.
    • Fire radiative power. detections had an invalid negative FRP value and are left out of FRP totals, but still counted as detections.
    • Countries and continents come from Natural Earth boundaries. Russia east of 60°E is counted in Asia rather than Europe. detections fell offshore and are excluded from country tables.
    • Confidence. VIIRS labels each detection low, nominal or high. High: , nominal: , low: . VIIRS keeps "high" for very strong, saturated fire pixels, so most detections are nominal. All levels count in totals; hotspots use nominal and high only.
    • October is partial (1st to 4th October only).
    • Data Source: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System), VIIRS NOAA-21 Collection 2 near-real-time active fire product, 375 m. Boundaries: Natural Earth. Prepared for the "Wildfire report" project.
